reviews.review:
This game is a blast. A shoot-em-up /beat em up.
Gratuitous violence, and is ultimately and bit camp and quite silly.
This is what gaming is all about.
Both colourful and fun.

For the Emperor, this and Dawn of War 1-2
Blood Ravens & Ultramarines.
Mod: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZuRunajkUe8

Man, Relic has been one great dev studio for ages.
Making Doom 2016 before Doom 2016, advancing push-forward combat in a genre that was content on squatting behind cover.
Relic has had a history of creating their own unique spin on things, with Homeworld 1&2, Impossible Creatures, Dawn of War 1&2, Company of Heroes, and Space Marine, a third person shooter with a heavy emphasis on melee and the way to stay alive is sometimes just going in to get those kills, as you heal through those executions that you get by stunning enemies.
Probably one of my favourite third person shooters.

Not a massive 40k fan, I sort of dig the cheese, the style, aesthetic, but haven't delved into much of anything, but it's apparent that Relic really knows their stuff.

I'm just so surprised by how restrained the game is visually in a time period when AAA have gone overboard with post processing and pixel packing. Relic stayed minimal where it's intended, baroque where it's intended, sprinkled in the appropriate amounts of blurs and blooms, and knew what mattered the most was making every explosion, blood bath, smoke puff and melee swing really feel comically excessive in the way Warhammer seems to lean into.
There's something about the lighting, shadows, shaders, surfaces, rendering, that also reminds me of Dead Space in the best sense.
I think it holds up visually really beautifully because they went in and used only what they needed and wanted, to achieve the intended artstyle.
Also have to just love the combat, the visual effects of blood spurts larger than the enemies themselves, the thick effects of bullet tracers, smoke trails, impact effects, dust, sparks, the lascannon beams and scorching decals, or melta guns cone of fire, the excellent sound design, just perfected all around.
Expect yourself to be sprinting into combat, charging and knocking down the hordes, coming out swinging your chainswords and poweraxes, dodging, ground stomping and jetpacking in many areas, stunning, comboing melee with AoE stuns, executing, throwing grenades, activating fury for multiple benefits (regen, instant easier execute, slowmo aiming) using ridiculously fun plasma weaponry, laserbeams, melting shotguns, bulky bolter machine guns.
Lots of attention to detail, in the effects, animations, hit feedback. Here's a small but fun one: When sprinting, not only is your Ultramarine animated in a fun way with that bulky comically massive armor, but the stomping sounds are great, and the subtle camera shake is just a cherry on top.
Animations, that gothic scifi-fantasy world and feel are also executed wonderfully.
Music is nothing unique, but still very well done, Relic has had pretty great music in all of their games.
Characters are exactly what you'd expect and hope for, cheesy, gravelly deep voices, stereotypical accents that just are required these days for Warhammer.
Also love the execution of the battlefields, they feel grand, with so much chaos and infighting between factions (guardsmen, orks, chaos) selling the planetary scale of events unfolding all around you.
Setpieces are hilariously over-the-top, just what you want from a 40k game.

Minor personal nitpicks that detract maybe 5% of overall enjoyment:
It's short! :'D 6-8 hour campaign. Still, short and sweet, with a decently told story, voice acting, cutscenes, pacing.
Final boss is a QTE. Not the worst one in execution, button prompts make sense and it looks fun, and I understand why they went with it.
Cliffhanger ending, makes sense and ends meaningfully, but I still wish for a sequel.
Maybe trim 5-10% of filler corridors hiding loading screens or used to pace combat encounters, they were in a few sections too long.
Not really a criticism, but the Chaos Space Marines felt bullet spongey, a bit harder to crack, still, makes sense, it's towards the end.
Only a couple of technical rough edges, in my 7hour replay I saw two small side areas where light was bleeding through geometry without any immediately apparent light source, and two cutscenes towards the ending had for a brief 1-2second period music triggers getting confused by the transition from combat to cutscene.
That's it, those are my nitpicks.

Game looks great, runs smoothly on my 6 year old potato laptop (i7-4710HQ, 12GB RAM, 840M 2GB VRAM, Win10x64bit, 60fps 85% of the time, only a handful of dips to 50, lowest 45fps), didn't need to fiddle with PCGamingWiki fixes though those exist, smooth setup.
I don't think I understand the appeal of this game. The story is non-existent, the shooting mechanics are generic at best, what's the draw here?
